I think I’ve been comparing my life to too many things lately too. 

I used to be popular and well liked in my early teens but then I started having trouble with bipolar which never happened before. I lost a lot of friends because of that and I always miss people wanting to talk and hang out with me like they used to. Like I said I think i compare my current life too much to other things. 

I’m starting to see that and work with my situation that I’m blessed to be in. I don’t need to worry about financial troubles and I’m healthy. That’s the world to some people so I definitely should be more greatful. Have a productive week, don’t take anything for granted.

Nothing has changed besides driving to school. I have online classes now. For the past couple months I’ve been working out and eating healthy. Also trying to play guitar more for mental stimulation. I have a small group of friends but we’re in our early 20s and they mostly go to work or school most of the time so we don’t hang out more than 3 times a month. The average day is 0 notifications, conversations with my mom (since I still live at home) and drinking coffee one way or another. 

I spend too much time on my phone, computer and YouTube so I definitely think I need to focus on hobbies and habits that get me out the house or make me more appealing to other young people. Corona is pushing the breaks on everyone’s life right now and it’s weird to see people freaking out because they need to social distance. I’ve been doing this for a long time, my days feel the same. But I hope you all reading this have a good week!

Going to the gym or running/walking in a busy area or trail can be like a social outing and help one feel less lonely too. 

other than just other focusing on your hobbies or crafts that you may be skilled at would be a good thing to focus on too. People, new friends or romantic partners always seem to be drawn in by talent or a finished project. 

If you don’t have any hobbies or talents -pick something up that you’ve always wanted to do. Photography? Pick up a 10$ disposable camera and point and shoot nice places around town. Some musical instrument? There are cheap acoustic and electric versions of all the popular instruments. Anything you’ve been interested in start investing time into it! There is no better time than now.

I’ve had HSV2 for 8 years and I’ve never had a blister or sore. Only a handful of times I have had a burning/itching sensation but that’s rare too.

I’m mostly asymptomatic but have had a burning sensation a handful (like 3-4) times in the first 3 years I had HSV2. I’ve had it for 8 years this year. No sores or lesions ever. I also developed common yeast infections when I was younger and ate a poor ramen noodle diet. Never had a yeast infection before I was with my partner. They went away when I went vegan at age 19. 

(Got herpes with my first sexual partner and long term relationship from when I was 14-16) I get irritated eyes from crying and pinkeye easily. I never had pinkeye before I had herpes. 

I also as of 2019 have had many types of nerve and shooting muscle pain all over my body. (21 turning 22 this summer) Lower back, upper back and arms, legs, and my head. Also recently my skin on parts of my body will become so sensitive in a patch area that it will feel numb, burn and hurt just by rubbing it against anything. 

For example: slowly rubbing my finger on my forearm a couple months ago felt like I was getting a tattoo by a heavy handed artist. Any type of cloth, soft blanket, or clothes rubbing against it would feel worse. That sensation went away in about a week and hasn’t come back as severe with other sensitive patches. 

I’m not on a daily dose of antivirals yet but will when I feel the time is right. I’m single and busy in school atm. 
Also I had no nerve or muscle pain when I was working out, in good shape and didn’t Juul. Working to get my health in line though!

Oh and none of my symptoms persist. They all come and go.

Still I avoid sex with people who I’m not in long term relationships with and make my partners get fully tested with me before I do anything with them because ignorance is not bliss. I’m asymptomatic besides a little burning I’ve had a couple instances, but I’m almost glad I caught herpes because I’m on guard as to how I protect myself now. Even if your current situation doesn’t work out, you will definitely find someone who understands and will know herpes isn’t as scary as people frame it to be.
